Condition a moderated network at a moderator value

Source: R/mgm_moderated.R
condition.Rd

Extracts the effective pairwise network implied by a moderated MGM (mgm_fit() with moderators) at a given value of the moderator, mirroring mgm::condition(): it applies the AND-rule pre-filter, absorbs the moderator value into the main-effect coefficients, and re-aggregates the pairwise edges.

Usage

condition(object, value, rule = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_moderated'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ..., value = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'psychnet_moderated'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A psychnet_moderated object from mgm_fit(..., moderators=).

value

A single moderator value to condition on: a level of a categorical moderator (number, label, factor or logical, as coded in the data), or a finite number on the raw scale of a continuous one.

rule

Symmetrization rule; defaults to the rule used at fit time.

x

A psychnet_moderated object.

row.names, optional

Standard as.data.frame() arguments; ignored.

...

Unused.

Value

condition() returns a psychnet network object (the moderator node carries no edges), with $mod_value the value conditioned on.

as.data.frame() on the moderated fit returns, with value = NULL, one row per pair of nodes joined by a main effect or a moderation effect, with columns from, to, main_effect (aggregated magnitude of the pairwise main effect, mgm convention: mean absolute nodewise estimate, zero when the pair does not survive rule), interaction (aggregated magnitude of the moderator x pair three-way interaction, NA for a pair that includes the moderator itself), moderated (logical: interaction > 0) and involves_moderator. With a value, it returns the tidy edge list (from, to, weight) of condition(x, value).

print() on the moderated fit shows the number of nodes, the moderator and the fit settings, and returns x invisibly.

Errors of class psychnet_bad_input when value is missing, not length one, not a level of a categorical moderator, or not a finite number for a continuous one.

Details

value is always read on the moderator's own scale. For a categorical moderator it is one of the levels observed in the data, in the coding the data used: 1/2 for a moderator coded 1/2, "treat" for a factor level "treat" (the internal 0-based level code is never exposed). For a continuous moderator it is a value on the raw scale; the moderator is standardized internally (mgm's scale = TRUE), and the value is mapped to (value - mean) / sd before conditioning, so value = mean(moderator) gives the network at the average moderator. (mgm::condition() instead takes the value on its internal standardized scale: condition(fit, v) here equals mgm::condition(ref, list(k = (v - mean) / sd)).)

Functions

  • as.data.frame(psychnet_moderated): Tidy table of the moderated fit: per-edge main and moderation effects, or (with value) the conditioned edge list.

  • print(psychnet_moderated): The moderated fit: nodes, moderator and settings.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x1 <- stats::rnorm(400); x2 <- stats::rnorm(400)
mod <- rep(1:2, each = 200)                 # moderator coded 1/2
y <- x1 * (mod == 2) + stats::rnorm(400)   # x1-y edge only when mod == 2
d <- data.frame(x1 = x1, x2 = x2, y = y, mod = mod)
fit <- mgm_fit(d, types = c("g", "g", "g", "c"), moderators = "mod")
fit
#> <psychnet_moderated> 4 nodes, moderator = mod
#>   gamma = 0.25, rule = AND, threshold = LW
#>   moderator levels: 1, 2
#>   as.data.frame(fit) for main and moderation effects; condition(fit, value) for the network at a moderator value.
as.data.frame(fit)            # main and moderation effects per edge
#>   from to main_effect interaction moderated involves_moderator
#> 1   x1  y           0   0.5665183      TRUE              FALSE
condition(fit, value = 1)     # no x1-y edge
#> <psychnet> mgm_moderated network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 0   (undirected)
condition(fit, value = 2)     # the x1-y edge appears
#> <psychnet> mgm_moderated network
#>   nodes: 4   edges: 1   (undirected)
as.data.frame(fit, value = 2) # the same network as a tidy edge list
#>   from to   weight
#> 1   x1  y 0.646064
